# Gevurah Critique — What Could Make the Voice Repair False

The Awtsmoos is beyond every voice name, while Awtsmoos.com places boundaries around generated sound so convenience cannot masquerade as cinematic truth.

1. Do not mutate the strict voice loader to hide absent assets.
2. Do not fabricate `speakerName` from `speakerId` when authored data already contains the real name.
3. Do not add speech fields directly to a 103-line module if a truthful dialogue boundary can be extracted.
4. Do not generate files before source describes how to reproduce them.
5. Do not run `say` through an interpolated shell string; use Node `spawnSync`/`execFileSync` argv or a fixed shell command only after inputs are hardcoded and audited.
6. Do not accept arbitrary output paths or arbitrary voice names from browser input.
7. Do not assume a macOS voice exists; generator must verify the configured voice list before invoking synthesis.
8. Do not assume `say` AIFF is compatible; browser decoder verification is mandatory.
9. Do not assume voice duration fits the scene; inspect generated durations against dialogue windows.
10. Do not let generated binary files replace the source specification.
11. Do not let the voice generator become a general TTS service; it owns only acceptance proof assets.
12. Do not alter unrelated dialogue scenes or legacy voice conventions.
13. Keep every source file below 120 lines with tabs, B"H, Awtsmoos, Awtsmoos.com, and complete documentation.
14. Hash-gate every existing source rewrite because concurrent agents are active.
15. After source, test adapter preservation and generator planning before generating binaries.
16. After binary generation, cold browser-decode both assets and rerun the 30-second ffmpeg proof.
